title: Criteria for the existence of modular inverse elements
summary: a has a multiplicative inverse modulo m if and only if gcd(a,m)=1.
applies: Integer modulo arithmetic; modulus greater than 1
aliases: The inverse element does not exist
detail: The inverse of 3 modulo 8 is 3 because 3×3 ≡ 1; 2 has no inverse modulo 8.
boundary: Ordinary division in the integer domain is not a substitute for modular division. The irreversibility of a certain denominator does not mean that the entire linear congruence equation has no solution.
relevance: Determine whether the denominator in the formula can be legally eliminated under the current modulus.
